# `silk/io/logger_console`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A `Logger` provider for browser and JavaScript hosts: `ConsoleLogger` hands each message to
the host's console.

## When to use
Provide `ConsoleLogger` for `Logger` in a `wasm32-unknown-unknown` program that runs in a
browser, Node.js, Deno or another JavaScript host. On WASI and native targets, use
`silk.io.logger_native` instead. Code that logs uses `silk.io.logger`, so a test can provide
`InMemoryLogger` instead.

## Details
The module imports one host function, `console` from the import module `silk`, and only a
program that provides `ConsoleLogger` imports it: a module that never logs this way keeps
importing nothing. The standard library's runner, `host/wasm-runner.mjs`, supplies the import.
It passes each message to `options.onLog` with its level, and by default to the console method
of the level: `console.debug` for trace and debug, `console.info`, `console.warn` and
`console.error`.

The import is `console(level, address, length, more)`. `level` counts from 0 for trace to 4 for
error, `address` and `length` name UTF-8 bytes in the module's memory, and `more` is 1 when the
next call continues the same message. The logger formats into a 256-byte buffer on the stack,
so a longer message arrives in several parts, which the host joins before it decodes them. The
logger does not allocate.

## Errors
None. A host cannot refuse a message.

## Gotchas
- The provider exists only on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- A host that instantiates the module itself supplies `silk.console`, or the instantiation fails.
- The logger adds no level, timestamp, or newline. The console shows the level by its method.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.logger { LogError, Logger }
import silk.io.logger_console { ConsoleLogger }

pub effect fn main() -> ()
  ! LogError {
  let mut logger = ConsoleLogger.make()
  let values = .{ name: "silk", count: 3 }

  // Calls `console.info("silk started 3 workers")` in the host.
  run Effect.logInfo("{name} started {count} workers", &values)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Logger>(&mut logger)
  return ()
}
```
